source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Signs Beholding Each Other, and of Equal Power
source_locator.short_quote: Such signs are also said to behold each other ... because each of them rises from one and the same part of the horizon, and sets in one and the same part.

prerequisites: two signs equally distant from a tropical sign
calculation_dependencies: equal distance from a tropical sign
comparison of horizon rise and set points

condition.relationship: equal distance from a tropical sign
condition.horizon_condition: rise and set at the same points

normalized_rule: Classify equally distant signs as beholding each other when they rise and set at the same parts of the horizon.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sign relationship, not a claim about interpersonal attention or visual perception.
review_notes: The equal-power and beholding descriptions are separate propositions. The editorial discussion of parallels in footnote 46 is not imported into this candidate.
transmission_notes: The rule is stated in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. Its meaning is limited to the source's sign relationship; later mundane-parallel terminology is excluded.
